newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-TOSHACK TO LEAVE DEPORTIVO CORUNA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TOSHACK TO LEAVE DEPORTIVO CORUNA.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna coach John Toshack has announced he will leave the club at the end of the season in the wake of a crucial defeat by Barcelona.

"I will not continue at Deportivo, whatever happens," said Toshack, who was heavily criticised along with Barcelona's Bobby Robson for the poor level of play in Saturday's match "With or without titles ... I will not stay on."

A veteran of the Spanish league after two spells at Real Sociedad and one at Real Madrid, Toshack has never looked comfortable at Deportivo, where the memory of successful former manager Arsenio Iglesias is still strong.
"Last year was a real Calvary for me...the supporters have always looked down on my work," said the Welshman.
Toshack's defensive instincts have drawn criticism after a close season in which Deportivo spent heavily to reinforce an already formidable squad.
Both Toshack and Robson have come under fire since Saturday's game.
"Ronaldo, Renaldo and Rivaldo and Figo, Guardiola, Sergi, Amunike Djukic...didn't produce a single gram of football," wrote a columnist in the daily 'El Pais' on Monday.
"Seen as an aim of science, that result, doubtless unachievable by the biochemists of the Pasteur Institute, was faithfully achieved by two farmhands from the British Museum," continued the article.
The media have also hit out at Robson for apparently encouraging striker Ronaldo to dive after a heavy challenge in the area.
Television viewers were treated to pictures of the former England manager imitating a diver on the touchline after the incident.

"Hey! But you're English" read a headline in the sports daily 'As' "(It was) curious that the Brazilian should practise the purest fair play and that the Englishman should ask for the opposite," continued the article.
Ronaldo's ability to ride heavy tackles and refusal to look for penalties was not the only aspect of his play to draw praise.
Most commentators have concluded that the match saw the re-emergence of the young striker, despite his failure to end a five-game goal-drought.
